/`.\n\n**Объявления:** каждый class/interface/trait/enum с FQCN, kind (`class|abstract-class|final-class|interface|trait|enum`), `extends`, `implements`, используемые traits, атрибуты типа, методы с видимостью (имена) — для member-уровня SchemaBuilder (там `define*` private) и для эвристики Eloquent (`extends` цепочка до `Illuminate\\Database\\Eloquent\\Model`, разрешается по индексу, внешние — по имени).\n\n**Ссылки (`references`)**, каждая: `file`, `symbol` (охватывающий `Class::method` / `Class` / ``), `kind`, `target`:\n| kind | Источник |\n|:--|:--|\n| `use` | `use` импорты (включая group use и function/const) |\n| `name` | любое разрешённое имя класса в коде: `new`, `::class`, static call/prop/const, `instanceof`, `catch`, типы параметров/возврата/свойств (включая union/nullable), атрибуты, `extends/implements/use trait` |\n| `fqcn-string` | строковый литерал, совпадающий с `/^\\\\?Vaulter\\\\[A-Za-z0-9_\\\\]+$/` (I1: FQCN-строки в конфиге и payload — тоже ссылки) |\n| `table` | строковый литерал, равный имени таблицы из identities/schema без префикса (`drives`, `nodes`, …) или с `v_`, в аргументе вызовов `table(`, `from(`, `join(`, `->table(`, `Schema::*(`, `DB::table(`, свойстве `$table`, а также в константах/массивах классов Schema/Repositories (без контекста — `table-literal`, слабее; сканы различают) |\n| `config` | первый аргумент `config(`, `Config::get(`, `->get(`/`->has(` на config-репозитории, если литерал начинается с `vaulter` (`vaulter.`, `vaulter-media.`, …) |\n| `route` | литерал-аргумент `route(`, `->name(`, `Route::has(`, `URL::route(` |\n| `probe` | вызовы `class_exists`, `interface_exists`, `enum_exists`, `trait_exists`, `function_exists`, `extension_loaded`, методы `->bound(`, `->resolved(` (любой получатель) — для I4; target = текст первого аргумента (pretty-print) |\n\nИмена разрешаются php-parser `NameResolver`. Пакет `collaboration` получает только `packages/documents/src/Collaboration/**` и JWT/hub-части (P5); `webhooks` — по ownership-map.\n- `action`: `keep` (остаётся на месте, тот же FQCN), `move` (другой пакет/FQCN), `split` (тип делится; обязательны `members` или `note` с частями), `replace` (заменяется новым механизмом P3, напр. `VaulterManager` → `Vaulter\\\\Drive\\\\Vaulter`), `delete` (без замены; только с `note`-причиной и ссылкой на решение).\n- `phase`: `P3` (меняется на месте механизмом ядра), `P4` (перенос владения), `P5` (коллаборация), `stay` (тип не меняется до freeze). `keep` ⇒ `stay` или `P3`; `move` ⇒ `P4|P5`.\n- `target_fqcn`: правило по умолчанию — `Vaulter\\\\` → `Vaulter\\\\\\\\`, где `` ∈ {`Media`,`Drive`,`Documents`,`Collaboration`,`Webhooks`}; сегмент, совпадающий с именем владельца, сразу после верхнего каталога удаляется (`Vaulter\\\\Models\\\\Drive\\\\Node` → `Vaulter\\\\Drive\\\\Models\\\\Node`, `Vaulter\\\\Contracts\\\\Webhooks\\\\X` → `Vaulter\\\\Webhooks\\\\Contracts\\\\X`). Для `keep` = `fqcn`. Особые цели (entry-point: `Vaulter\\\\Drive\\\\Vaulter`, `Vaulter\\\\Drive\\\\Facades\\\\Vaulter`; `withoutTenancy` → `Vaulter\\\\Tenancy\\\\Tenancy::without`) — явные fqcn-правила. Уникальность `target_fqcn` и отсутствие коллизии с существующим другим типом целевого пакета проверяются генератором.\n- `surface` — предложение для P3 по D27/architecture#api-surface: `Api`, `Spi:Implement`, `Spi:Call`, `Internal`, `undecided` (только с `note`, попадает в findings как вход P3). Ориентиры: фасады/entry/ServiceProvider-классы хоста/Testing-кит → Api; Contracts, которые хост реализует или регистрирует (драйверы, сканеры, резолверы, sinks) → Spi:Implement; контракты, которые модули вызывают у ядра → Spi:Call или Api; Data/ValueObjects/Enums/Exceptions, видимые из Api-сигнатур → Api; Models (Eloquent), Actions, Repositories, Http/Controllers, Console-команды, Jobs, Doctor-проверки, Providers/*Registrar → Internal (CLI/HTTP — поверхность идентичностей, не PHP API). Типы, перечисленные в текущих `packages/*/tests/Arch/__snapshots__` PublicApiSnapshotTest, не могут получить `Internal` без `note` (это текущий baseline).\n- `eloquent: true` для моделей (цепочка extends до Eloquent Model) — нужна I9/D27.\n\n**Правила `Fixtures/target-map/rules/.json`:**\n```json\n{\"scope\":[\"Vaulter\\\\Access\\\\\"],\"rules\":[\n {\"match\":\"prefix\",\"value\":\"Vaulter\\\\Access\\\\\",\"owner\":\"drive\",\"action\":\"move\",\"phase\":\"P4\",\"surface\":\"Internal\",\"why\":\"architecture#ownership-map Access\"},\n {\"match\":\"fqcn\",\"value\":\"Vaulter\\\\ValueObjects\\\\Access\\\\Actor\",\"owner\":\"core\",\"action\":\"keep\",\"phase\":\"P3\",\"surface\":\"Api\",\"why\":\"ядро оставляет Actor\"},\n {\"match\":\"file\",\"value\":\"packages/core/database/migrations/2026_10_13_000002_create_v_nodes_table.php\",\"owner\":\"drive\",\"role\":\"migration\",\"phase\":\"P4\",\"why\":\"v_nodes — drive\"},\n {\"match\":\"member\",\"value\":\"Vaulter\\\\Schema\\\\SchemaBuilder::defineNodes\",\"owner\":\"drive\",\"action\":\"move\",\"phase\":\"P4\",\"why\":\"доменный DDL\"}\n]}\n```\nПоля правила необязательны кроме match/value/owner/why; отсутствующие берутся по умолчанию (`action` = keep при owner = текущему пакету, иначе move; `phase` = stay/P4; `surface` = `undecided`). **Приоритет:** `fqcn` > `prefix` (длиннейший) ; два prefix равной длины, совпавшие с одним типом, или два одинаковых `value` в разных файлах — ошибка. **Полнота:** каждый тип из SourceIndex ровно одно итоговое правило; каждый файл без объявлений типов (миграции, конфиги, маршруты, фабрики-классы тоже типы) — `file`-правило; каждый метод `Vaulter\\\\Schema\\\\SchemaBuilder` любой видимости (`define*` — private) — `member`-правило. **Устаревшее правило** (ничего не выбрало как победитель) — ошибка. Пакеты кроме core покрываются простыми prefix-правилами `keep/stay` своего namespace плюс исключения (documents Collaboration → collaboration P5; media BlobStore::attach/detach → member-правила split в drive link service по ownership-map).\n\n**Зоны ответственности файлов правил (`scope`).** Каждый rules-файл объявляет `\"scope\": [...]` — FQCN-префиксы (`Vaulter\\\\Access\\\\`), точные FQCN и пути-префиксы файлов (`path:packages/core/database/`). Ответственный файл для типа/файла — тот, чей элемент `scope` совпадает **длиннейшим** образом; равная длина в двух файлах — ошибка. Генератор проверяет: (1) каждый тип/файл/член, за который отвечает файл, выбран правилом **этого** файла; (2) правило файла не выбирает ничего вне его scope; (3) объединение scope покрывает всё. Так файлы правил делятся между параллельными units без пересечений. `inventory.php target-map --report --rules=` печатает пробелы/конфликты/устаревшие правила только этого файла и выходит 1, если они есть (проверка unit); полный `--check` требует всех файлов и совпадения target-map.json.\n\n**Разбиение core (P2.2 units):** `core-access-sharing` (доступ, роли/гранты, шаринг — всё в drive кроме ядерного Actor/MissingActorException), `core-drive` (дерево, модели/репозитории Drive, профили, хендлеры, naming, квоты, активность, журнал изменений, entry-point VaulterManager/Facades), `core-content-media-webhooks` (Cas → media, Content → media|drive по D28, Webhooks → webhooks, Outbox/relay → core), `core-kernel` (scope `Vaulter\\\\` и `path:packages/core/` — остаток: каркас и смешанные каталоги Doctor/Configuration/Console/Http/Providers/Schema/Support/Testing/Exceptions/Data/Enums/ValueObjects/Events, файлы core/database|config|routes, члены SchemaBuilder). Точные scope-списки — в units пункта P2.2.\n\n**Filament model reads:** все ссылки (`use`/`name`) из `packages/filament/src/**` на типы с `eloquent: true` → `consumers.filament_model_reads` (дедуп по file+symbol+model). `replacement` одинаковый: P4 authorized drive listing/lookup API и snapshots (source-review#code-facts «Точка входа/ORM», I9).\n\n**Артефакт плана:** `@plan/artifacts/P2.2/type-map.md` — сводка: число типов по (package → owner, action, phase, surface), список `split/replace/delete/undecided` поимённо, коллизии/спорные решения с причиной. Он генерируется из JSON вручную/скриптом; источник истины — JSON." }, { "id": "identities", "title": "Модель инвентаря идентичностей (P2.3)", "text": "Пять сгенерированных файлов `tests/Repo/Arch/Fixtures/identities/.json` + ручные правила владения `identities/owners/.json` (формат как у type-map rules: `match` ∈ `exact|prefix|glob`, `value`, `owner`, `why`; приоритет exact > длиннейший prefix > glob; полнота и устаревшие правила — ошибка). Канонический preset для деталей: `bigint.string.v.off` на каждом engine; затем по всем 48 preset × 3 engine проверить, что набор таблиц/колонок/индексов/FK тот же по логическому имени (префикс `custom_`→`v_`, типы id меняются по оси ids — разрешено), а отличия по осям `tenancy` (колонки tenant_*) и `host_keys` записываются как `variants`. NodeTraverser replaces a node with the visitor's return value during enterNode, but continues traversing children of that replacement. This means if NameResolver mutates a Name node into a FullyQualified node during enterNode, the second visitor would see the resolved node instead of the original.

If NameResolver resolves names lazily in leaveNode, IndexVisitor would see unresolved Name nodes and miss them because onName only handles FullyQualified. The author needs to check the NameResolver source to confirm when resolution occurs. A group-use bug was also noted: if the prefix is resolved but items remain unresolved, the visitor may concatenate them incorrectly.

A concrete double-resolution bug was identified for group-use statements. If NameResolver converts the UseItem name to a fully qualified class name, concatenating it with a resolved prefix like `Foo\Bar` yields `Foo\Bar\Foo\Bar\Baz`. This would be a serious bug.

Call detection timing is also being questioned. `onString` runs in `enterNode`, so the call node's name may not yet be resolved when the parent stack is inspected.

Call detection timing is resolved. The call node is entered before the string, so NameResolver has already processed it, and `isConfigCall` uses `getLast()` to extract the function name without requiring full resolution.

A design gap was noted for table references inside constants and arrays of Schema/Repositories classes: these should be recorded as `table-literal` without context.

The `inTableClass` regex requires a trailing backslash, so it only matches classes nested inside a `Schema` or `Repositories` namespace. A class literally named `Schema` outside that namespace would be missed.

The `inTableClass` regex is confirmed to match classes nested inside `Schema` or `Repositories` namespaces, such as `Vaulter\Schema\SchemaBuilder`.

A bug was found in the `$table` property detection. The visitor checks if the parent node is a `PropertyItem` and its name equals `'table'`. This correctly catches plain properties like `public $table = 'nodes'`. However, promoted properties or typed properties such as `public string $table = 'nodes'` may have a different AST structure, so the parent might not be a `PropertyItem` at all. In those cases the string would not be recognized as a table reference.

The `$table` property check is confirmed to work for promoted and typed properties, since the parent node remains a `PropertyItem`.

A design gap was found in config call detection. The implementation only recognizes `config(` and `Config::get(` as config calls, but the design document also requires detecting `->get(` and `->has(` on any config repository object.

The config-call detection is too broad. It treats any `->get(` or `->has(` call on any object as a config reference, not just on a config repository. This creates false positives for calls like `$request->has('vaulter.x')` or `$cache->get('vaulter.foo')`. The code also does not verify that the string value starts with `vaulter.` or `vaulter-media.`.

The prefix check only requires the string to start with `vaulter`, not a specific config repository. The `Config::get` match is overly broad because it accepts any class ending in `Config`, not just `Illuminate\Support\Facades\Config`. `Config::set` is correctly excluded.

The broad `->get` and `->has` config detection is a spec deviation that risks false `config` references and false new violations in I1. A reproduction will be prepared. Route call handling is now being examined.

Route call detection is also too broad. The implementation matches any `->name(` or `->route(` call on any object, not just on a Route or URL repository. This creates false positives for calls like `$request->name('vaulter.x')`. The design document only requires detecting `route(`, `->name(`, `Route::has`, and `URL::route`.

The `->name(` false positive is severe: `$user->name('foo')` or `$this->name('something')` in a controller would both be misclassified as route references. `Route::name('foo')` is also incorrectly matched, though that call pattern is less common. The first-argument check for route names inside method chains like `Route::get(...)->name('vaulter.x')` is correct.

The design document literally requires detecting `->name(` on any object, so the broad `->name(` match is actually a spec deviation rather than a false positive. The implementation also adds `->route(` beyond the spec. `Route::get` URI arguments are correctly excluded because the default branch only matches `name` or `route`.

Probe detection is too broad. The implementation matches `->bound(` and `->resolved(` on any object, but the design document only requires detecting these methods when called on a config repository.

Function name resolution is correct. `class_exists` is a PHP internal function, so NameResolver resolves it to `\class_exists`, and `callParts` extracts the correct unqualified name via `getLast()`.

A namespaced `class_exists` function would still be flagged as a probe call. The probe target is correctly set to the pretty-print of the first argument, including empty targets. A double recording bug was noted: `class_exists(Foo::class)` records both a probe reference and a name reference to `Foo`.

The pretty-printed probe target for `class_exists(Foo::class)` may include a leading backslash, but this is acceptable. The dynamic-name detection correctly identifies `$class::method()` as a `dynamic` reference.

The dynamic-name check also catches `new $class`, `$class::CONST`, `$class::$prop`, and `$x instanceof $class`. These are extra beyond the spec's `$class::` example, but reasonable. A type-safety bug was found: `Name` nodes are not instances of `Expr`, so static calls like `Foo::bar()` are correctly excluded from the dynamic list.

`new static` and `new self` are correctly excluded from dynamic references because they resolve to Name nodes rather than Expr. The dynamic list is stored separately from the main references, matching the design. The symbol for a dynamic class is resolved at enterNode time, but the method stack may not yet contain the current method name when onDynamicClass runs.

The dynamic class symbol is correctly resolved because the enclosing method is already on the stack when `onDynamicClass` runs. A new concern was raised: name references may be missed if NameResolver does not convert certain names to `FullyQualified`.

A potential bug was identified in how NameResolver handles name resolution timing. If it replaces nodes during leaveNode rather than enterNode, the visitor would see unresolved Name nodes and miss references. The developer plans to inspect NameResolver's source code to verify this.

Function imports via `use function` statements are recorded as use references.

Function imports via `use function` are unlikely to cause false I1 positives because non-Vaulter classes do not match the PSR-4 prefix. Group use statements for functions still need verification. Relative names should be fully qualified by NameResolver, but the tests must confirm this behavior. Attribute name resolution also needs inspection.

Trait use adaptations and `insteadof` precedence are handled correctly. Trait aliases are identifiers, not class names, so they are not recorded as references. Anonymous classes extending other classes are properly attributed to the enclosing symbol. Enum implements and interface extends are also covered. The `isEloquent` check only inspects the first `extends` clause, which is sufficient for PHP classes and interfaces.

The Eloquent detection logic incorrectly treats `Pivot`, `MorphPivot`, and `User` as valid base classes. The design document only requires extending `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model`. This extension risks false positives for classes that do not actually inherit from Eloquent.

The Eloquent extension to User, Pivot, and MorphPivot is a spec deviation. The design document explicitly requires the chain to stop at Model. External parents are checked only by name. A class extending User is not an Eloquent model under the strict specification.

The Eloquent deviation is medium severity. It causes extra false positives in downstream checks rather than missed models, because Pivot and MorphPivot are themselves Eloquent models.

The `packageOf` helper uses a longest-prefix match, so `Vaulter\Media\` correctly takes precedence over `Vaulter\Media`. However, the prefix check uses `str_starts_with` without a trailing slash, which causes false matches like `Vaulter\ModelsExtra` when the intended prefix is `Vaulter\Models`.

The `packageOf` prefix sort breaks ties alphabetically when two prefixes have equal length, which is unspecified in the design document. Duplicate fully-qualified class names are silently ignored because the first declaration wins. The cache key for migration tables is sensitive to argument ordering, so unsorted table lists produce different cache entries.

The JSON encoder does not sort arrays. The design document requires lists to be ordered by entity key, but the implementation keeps them in insertion order.

The JSON encoder intentionally preserves list order, so generators must sort their arrays before encoding. The packages generator is the first candidate to inspect for this requirement. Allowlist comparison keys are view, file, symbol, kind, and target.

Allowlist comparison sums counts for identical keys. Pre-aggregated violations are accepted, but duplicate entries in the same batch would double-count. A stale count bug was also noted: if a key is missing from the found set, the difference is computed against zero.

Count mismatches are correctly treated as stale violations rather than new ones. The allowlist key excludes target_owner, and reason and removed_in are mandatory fields. Removed_in values are restricted to P3, P4, P5, or never.

The implementation does not validate that `removed_in` is less than or equal to the invariant's blocking phase. The design document requires this check for Allowlist semantics, so this gap may be a P2.1 finding.

The explicit checklist for this item omits the phase ordering constraint. The full design document still requires `removed_in` to be at or before the invariant's blocking phase. I am checking whether tests cover this validation.

The removed_in phase ordering gap is confirmed as a semantic bug. I1 blocks from P4, so removed_in must be P3 or P4; I4 blocks from P3, so removed_in must be P3. The implementation accepts any of P3, P4, P5, or never without enforcing this constraint. Severity is medium.

The removed_in phase ordering gap is a spec deviation. I will provide a reproduction showing an I1 entry with removed_in P5 is accepted.

The removed_in phase ordering gap is a real semantic hole. Accepting an overly late removal date means the allowlist will miss violations that outlive the blocking phase. Severity is medium/low.

Category is not required for all entries, only for `never`. Duplicate entries throw as expected. Block mode correctly enforces an empty allowlist.

The pipe separator in allowlist keys could cause collisions if any field value contains a pipe. This is unlikely but plausible.

Rules priority correctly ranks exact fqcn, file, and member matches above prefix matches by longest prefix length.

A bug was found in prefix tie-breaking: when two prefixes have equal length, the first encountered wins because the comparison only updates when rank is strictly greater.

The design document requires an error when two equal-length prefixes both match the same type. The implementation only rejects duplicate exact matches across files. It silently keeps the first rule when two different prefixes of equal length both match one type.

The equal-length prefix tie-breaking bug is a false alarm. A fully qualified class name cannot start with two different prefixes of the same length, so the silent first-match behavior is unreachable in practice.

The prefix tie-breaking concern is resolved. Identical rules in the same file are caught by the duplicate-value check, so equal-length prefixes cannot produce a silent conflict in practice.

Scope matching has a bug. Path scopes only match file subjects, but non-path scopes match both type and member subjects. A prefix like `Vaulter\Schema\` therefore incorrectly matches member keys such as `Vaulter\Schema\SchemaBuilder::defineNodes`.

Exact FQCN scopes match too broadly. A scope like `Vaulter\Access\Foo` matches the type key itself, but also incorrectly matches `Vaulter\Access\FooExtra` and `Vaulter\Access\Foo\Bar` because `str_starts_with` does not enforce a trailing slash.

The exact FQCN scope bug is confirmed. The design document requires exact FQCN scopes to match only the exact class name, but the implementation uses `str_starts_with` for all non-path scopes. This causes an exact scope like `Vaulter\Access\Foo` to incorrectly match `Vaulter\Access\FooBar` and `Vaulter\Access\Foo\Child`.

Exact member scopes such as `Vaulter\Schema\SchemaBuilder::defineNodes` also incorrectly match longer names like `defineNodesExtra`. File path scopes without a trailing slash match paths like `database_extra` or `database-old`, though callers likely use trailing slashes. A rule selecting outside its scope is also being examined.

The out-of-scope check is skipped when a scope tie occurs, because the winner is null and the tie is already an error. A rule that matched but lost to a higher-priority rule is correctly flagged as stale. When a subject itself is a tie, the winner is still computed and recorded.

Invalid rules are rejected before they can become stale. Duplicate-value conflicts correctly use `explode('|', $key, 2)`, so pipe characters inside values are handled safely. Identical rules in the same file are treated as conflicts, which is stricter than the specification requires. A scope tie within a single file is also being examined.

A rule file correctly flags subjects owned by other files as out-of-scope. Identical rules in the same file do not create a scope tie, because the file is counted only once.

The out-of-scope check only flags a rule that actually wins. A lower-priority rule in file A matching a subject owned by file B is not flagged as selecting outside scope, because file B's rule wins. The implementation correctly checks the winning rule's file against the subject's owner.

A prefix rule shorter than the scope can match types outside that scope. For example, `Vaulter\Access\` matches types under `Vaulter\Access\Foo\` even though it is shorter than the exact scope `Vaulter\Access\Foo\`.

The Rules class does not apply the default values specified in the design document. Missing action fields default to keep when the owner is the current package, otherwise move. Missing phase fields default to stay or P4. Missing surface fields default to undecided.

The missing default values are not a P2.1 bug. The Rules class only judges rules and stores match, value, owner, and why; it does not build the full type-map entry. Default action, phase, and surface values are applied later by the generator in P2.2.

The exact FQCN boundary bug is the real issue. Prefixes without trailing slashes also match unrelated namespaces, but the specification examples include trailing slashes, so this is a footgun rather than a spec deviation.

The exact FQCN scope bug is confirmed as a spec deviation. The design document explicitly requires exact FQCNs to match only the precise class name, yet the implementation uses `str_starts_with` for all non-path scopes. Prefixes without trailing slashes are merely a footgun because the specification examples include trailing backslashes.

The `winner()` method silently returns the first of two identical fqcn rules with the same value. Both rules remain in `$this->rules`, so the winner is not deterministic.

The equal-length prefix conflict is impossible for distinct strings. Unicode normalization does not change this. The existing test likely uses identical prefixes, so the duplicate check already catches it.

Scope ties are limited to identical scope prefixes across different files. The implementation correctly records both matches in `$best` when this occurs.

A critical finding concerns NameResolver and visitor order.

NameResolver mutates child nodes in place during the parent's enterNode. IndexVisitor then sees the already-resolved names when it enters them later. The visitor order is correct.

I am reading `NameContext::getResolvedClassName` to understand a critical bug.

NameResolver mutates child nodes to FullyQualified during the parent's enterNode. IndexVisitor then traverses those already-resolved children. Attribute names and property types are fully resolved before IndexVisitor ever visits them.

Trait use adaptations are fully resolved before IndexVisitor visits them, so they are recorded correctly. The parent context on the stack is available when the FullyQualified child is visited. Now examining the SKIP logic.

The SKIP logic correctly excludes function names, constant fetches, and use items. Static call class names and attribute names are properly recorded. A GROUP USE bug was spotted in `useItems` string concatenation.

NameResolver does not fully qualify UseItem names or GroupUse prefixes. Aliases are added to the context, but the prefix stays as written in the source. This means `use Foo\Bar\{Baz}` records `Foo\Bar\Baz`, which is correct since use statements always resolve from the global namespace. However, `use \Foo\Bar\{Baz}` may produce a prefix of `Foo\Bar` because Name::toString() strips leading backslashes.

All use imports are absolute, so the group-use prefix bug is harmless. Aliases are correctly recorded as the imported fully qualified class name.

I will write a probe script to hunt for real bugs.

A likely bug surfaced: `self`, `parent`, and `static` are not resolved by NameResolver, so they remain as plain Name nodes. IndexVisitor only records FullyQualified names, meaning these special class references are silently missed.

The missing `self`, `static`, and `parent` references are intentional. Tests explicitly expect them to be absent from name targets, and the design doc requires php-parser NameResolver to handle resolution.

Trait `use` declarations may be silently omitted from name references. The test expects trait names to appear in `extends`, `instanceof`, and `catch` contexts, but a trait used via `use` would not be counted. This would cause the expected name counts to fail.

A critical visitor-order bug is suspected. NameResolver resolves child names before IndexVisitor processes the parent, so when IndexVisitor::onName sees a FullyQualified node, its stack parent may not yet reflect the resolved context.

Attribute names are fully resolved during the attributed node's enterNode, so the stack parent is already correct when IndexVisitor records them. Property types are also resolved in place on the Property node itself, not inside its children, so they should be captured properly.

Function and method parameter types are resolved before child traversal, so their FullyQualified names are recorded with the correct parent. Nullable types in `new` expressions are already handled. Group-use prefixes are absolute paths and do not require namespace-relative resolution.

Group-use aliases and relative prefixes concatenate correctly. Unqualified function names inside namespaces are not resolved by NameResolver, so they are properly excluded from name references.

Imported constants are silently skipped. NameResolver resolves `LIMIT` to `Vaulter\LIMIT`, but IndexVisitor ignores the resulting FullyQualified name because its parent is a `ConstFetch`. The constant reference is therefore omitted from name targets.

The `ConstFetch` exclusion is correct. Constants are not class names, so skipping them prevents false positives like `true`, `false`, and `null`. Class constants such as `SomeClass::class` are recorded via `ClassConstFetch`.

FuncCall names are skipped, but this is safe because PHP 8 forbids calling classes as functions. New_ expressions and union or nullable type contexts correctly record their FullyQualified class names. Attribute arguments such as `Bar::class` inside `#[Foo(Bar::class)]` are also captured properly.

The table-detection list includes `on`, which the design document omits. This risks false positives when `on` receives a table name instead of a column.

The `Schema::*(` pattern is implemented correctly: any Schema method call with a string argument is treated as a table reference. The design document only lists `Schema::table`, but the code accepts all Schema methods. The `DB::table` pattern is also incorrectly expanded to match any `DB::*` method, not just `DB::table`.

Named arguments such as `entity: 'drives'` are correctly treated as table references, since the design document explicitly includes them.

The `on` table-detection entry is a likely false positive. The design document omits it, and real code rarely passes table names to `on`. The `DB::table` wildcard is also suspect: the spec requires only that exact call, yet the code matches any `DB::*` method. These extra matches risk false table references.

Config-detection is too broad. The design requires the receiver to be a config repository, but the implementation matches any `->get` or `->has` call. This risks false positives from unrelated objects.

The phrase "на config-репозитории" is ambiguous. It may describe the `->get`/`->has` pattern rather than filter calls by receiver type.

Only the first positional argument of `config()` and `Config::get` is checked. Named arguments like `key: 'vaulter.x'` are ignored, so they will not match.

The `isConfigCall` check for static calls only verifies the class name ends in `Config`. It does not require the method to be `get`, so any static call on a class named `Config` would be treated as a config reference.

The `isConfigCall` logic is more permissive than the design document. It records any static call where the class ends in `Config`, so `Config::set`, `Config::has`, or even `Something\Config::anything` would all match as config references. The spec only requires `Config::get`. Route detection is correct: the design explicitly allows any `->name(` call.

The `fqcn-string` regex `/^\\\\?Vaulter\\\\[A-Za-z0-9_\\\\]+$/` is too permissive. It matches invalid paths like `Vaulter\123` and `Vaulter\`, so it cannot reliably distinguish valid class names from garbage.

The `fqcn-string` regex matches trailing backslashes after `Vaulter\`, so strings like `Vaulter\` or `Vaulter\Drive\` are incorrectly accepted as valid fully-qualified names.

A symbol attribution bug was found in anonymous class methods. A `new \Vaulter\Media\Blob()` call inside an anonymous class is incorrectly attributed to the outer method `Outer::foo` instead of the anonymous class's own method `Outer::bar`. This would mislabel symbols in the inventory.

Arrow functions, property defaults, enums, and traits are all correctly attributed to their enclosing symbols. The anonymous-class attribution bug is now confirmed as a real issue.

References inside `match` arms and `if` expressions are handled correctly as method-level expressions. Promoted constructor property types resolve to the constructor method, matching the spec's requirement that references belong to their enclosing method.

Relative class names resolved by NameResolver are correctly captured as fully-qualified references. `class_alias` and `is_a`/`is_subclass_of` are not treated as probes, which aligns with the spec. The probe pattern correctly records both the function call and the class name inside its argument.

FullyQualified names correctly include the leading backslash in probe output. Dynamic `instanceof` and `new ($expr)` expressions are treated as dynamic references, which is acceptable because they belong to a separate list and do not appear in scans.

`parent::` static calls are not recorded as name references. NameResolver does not resolve `parent` to the parent class, so `parent::boot()` is invisible to scans. This risks missing cross-package dependencies.

The `parent::` reference is a false negative. A missed dependency can be stale if previously allowlisted, or new if absent from scans. The design explicitly mandates using php-parser NameResolver for name resolution, so the lack of `parent` resolution is acceptable.

Trait `insteadof` names are correctly resolved and recorded as extra name references.

Group-use prefixes are correctly resolved as absolute names, so relative prefixes do not create incorrect leading namespaces. UseItem nodes contain a Name node, which risks double-recording the same use name.

The double-recording concern for UseItem nodes is resolved. FullyQualified names are skipped by onName because the parent is UseItem, so useItems records them once. Relative names are not FullyQualified, so onName ignores them and useItems captures them correctly. Use statements are at file level, so no class-level symbol attribution applies.

Multiple namespaces in one file are handled correctly. NameResolver assigns each declaration the proper namespacedName. Files without a namespace resolve relative class names to bare identifiers.

The `onName` parent check for names that are the class of a `StaticCall` is correct. The stack top is the `StaticCall`, so the name is not skipped and gets recorded. There is no double-visit bug here: after NameResolver replaces `$node->class` with a `FullyQualified`, the child node is visited and recorded properly.

PHP 8.4 property hooks are not ClassMethod nodes, so references inside their bodies may be attributed to the class symbol instead of a specific hook. This would merge hook-level references into the class count and produce incorrect inventory totals.

First-class callables such as `Foo::bar(...)` are correctly recorded as StaticCall nodes, so their class names are captured. The reviewer then began examining attribute name resolution with `self`, but the thought was cut off.

DNF types such as `(A&B)|C` are correctly handled because PHP-Parser represents them as UnionType nodes containing IntersectionType, and resolveType recurses into both. Primitive keywords like `false`, `true`, `null`, `void`, `never`, `mixed`, `self`, `parent`, and `static` appear as Identifier nodes rather than Name nodes, so they are not recorded as type references. The reviewer then began examining whether special type keywords might still be misclassified as Name nodes.

`self` in return type hints is not recorded as a name reference, which is acceptable because it only refers to the current class. `parent` in return type hints is also missed, matching the earlier `parent::` issue. Allowlist counts merge violations that differ only by target_owner because the spec key excludes that field. This is acceptable.

Prefix conflicts are impossible for equal-length string prefixes. If two prefixes match the same subject key, they must be identical.

A reproduction confirms a bug in exact FQCN scope matching. The `exact` scope `Vaulter\Access\Actor` is evaluated with `str_starts_with`, so it incorrectly matches `Vaulter\Access\ActorExtra`. This causes the wrong rule to apply to unrelated classes.

The exact FQCN scope bug is confirmed as a real semantic violation. This produces a false out-of-scope error where the wide prefix rule wins. The same boundary failure occurs for `Vaulter\Access\Actor\Child`.

The reviewer proposes a convention to distinguish exact FQCN from prefix scopes: a trailing backslash indicates a prefix, while a bare class name indicates an exact match. This would allow the implementation to stop using `str_starts_with` for exact FQCNs and prevent false ownership claims.

The existing tests do not exercise exact FQCN scope matching, so the prefix-matching bug remains latent. If the design is strictly followed, exact FQCNs must match by equality rather than string prefix.

The stale-rule logic is correct. A prefix rule is only stale if it selects no winner; a longer prefix that wins over its subjects does not make the shorter one obsolete.

Exact class scopes match members via `str_starts_with` because the member key begins with the class name plus `::`. This may be intentional or a bug.

The reviewer is weighing whether exact FQCN scopes should match members. If exact matching uses equality, a class scope like `Vaulter\Schema\SchemaBuilder` would not cover its methods. The spec requires the longest scope match, so the implementation must decide whether to treat exact class names as prefix matches or require separate member scopes.

The reviewer concludes that exact FQCN scope matching members is a reasonable extension. The real bug is the false ownership claim on unrelated classes like `ActorExtra`. Path prefixes should match file paths on segment boundaries.

A `only` filter bug is confirmed. Uncovered problems have an empty files list, so they are hidden when `--only` is set because `in_array($only, [], true)` returns false. Scope-tie and out-of-scope problems still include both files and remain visible.

The reviewer reconsiders the `--only` filter bug. Uncovered subjects have an empty files list, so filtering by file drops them. This may be acceptable because uncovered items belong to no file. The `--only` filter behavior is acceptable. Uncovered global gaps are hidden from unit reports because they belong to no file. Conflicts and stale rules remain visible since they list affected files.

Invalid-rule problems are correctly shown under `--only` because they list the affected file. Duplicate files in match or value conflicts are deduplicated. The CLI exit-code logic is sound: a generator returning 2 sets the final exit to 2, and a later generator returning 0 cannot lower it.

PHP 8.2 readonly classes are treated as standard classes, which aligns with the spec's declaration kinds.

`DB::table()` correctly registers a table reference. `->join()` and `Schema::create()` also register tables properly, while `->where()` is correctly skipped. A potential false positive exists: `->on()` matches because `on` is in TABLE_CALLS, but the spec omits it, so this needs verification against the codebase.

Closures do not change the enclosing method symbol, so table references inside them still correctly attribute to the parent method. A `$table` property defined in a trait or parent class is only recorded as a reference in that parent's source file; subclasses that inherit it without overriding it will not register a separate reference.

A string literal inside a class constant such as `public const ALL = ['nodes', 'v_drives']` is correctly flagged as a table-literal reference because the class context remains active. However, table-literal detection may also fire for table names appearing in method bodies of Schema classes that are not part of an actual table-call context.

The spec's "без контекста" requirement means table-literal references should only be recorded inside class constants and arrays, not inside method bodies. The current code incorrectly flags any string equal to a table name inside a Schema or Repositories class as a table-literal, including strings in method bodies, exception messages, and comparisons.

Config references are only detected when the argument is positional, so named arguments like `config(key: 'vaulter.x')` are missed. Nullsafe calls are handled correctly. `static::method()` is not recorded as a name reference because the `static` keyword is not a resolved expression.

Variable variables like `$$c` are correctly skipped. A string literal used as a class name in a static call, such as `('Vaulter\\Foo')::method()`, is properly handled because String_ extends Expr and satisfies the dynamic class check.

Class attributes are correctly recorded as name references, including the attribute class itself. Group-use declarations resolve qualified names by prepending the import prefix, so `Cas\Hasher` becomes `Vaulter\Media\Cas\Hasher`. A leading backslash in a group-use alias is stripped during prefix assembly.

Function group-use declarations resolve correctly, for example `Vaulter\helper`. The alias builder does not modify AST nodes, so use items cannot be double-prefixed. Relative names in traits, enums, and interfaces are handled by the same NameResolver logic. A catch clause such as `catch (\Exception $e)` is recorded as the name `Exception`.

The reviewer is checking whether `implements` clauses are recorded as name references. The existing union test does not assert this, so a script will be run to verify.

`onName` skips names whose parent is a `FuncCall`, which correctly excludes first-class callables. Anonymous classes nested inside methods are recorded with the method symbol because the method stack remains active.

References inside anonymous class methods are incorrectly attributed to a nonexistent symbol such as `Outer::anonMethod`. Nested anonymous classes make the symbol even more invalid. The reviewer will reproduce this bug.

Anonymous classes at file level collapse all methods to the `<file>` symbol because `currentClass` is null. Methods inside anonymous classes are also wrongly attributed to the outer class. The reviewer will reproduce this.

File-level functions correctly collapse to the `<file>` symbol. Interface constants and enum case values are recorded under the correct class symbol. Attribute arguments containing `new` expressions are also captured properly.

The reviewer is checking whether the design document explicitly requires allowlist phase ordering. They will include this finding only if the spec is unambiguous and a clear reproduction exists.

Two same-length prefixes matching the same type are impossible, so that case is skipped. Conflicts between fqcn rules with identical values in the same file are correctly raised. Match data collisions in the `seen` set are not a concern because the match content is controlled.

Prefix matching is case-sensitive, but the codebase uses consistent FQCN casing so this is acceptable. Scope matching via `str_starts_with` is also case-sensitive. File rules require exact path matches, and member rules require exact value matches.

Prefix rules are correctly limited to file subjects, since files without type declarations need file rules. A type subject cannot be classified by a file rule. When a scope tie occurs and the owner is null, the out-of-scope check is skipped, but the winning rule may still come from one of the tied files, so this is acceptable. An empty subject list causes all rules to be stale.

The `resolve([])` test is correct. It expects only invalid-rule codes because all three rules are invalid and none are added, so no stale rules are produced.

The `only` filter correctly drops problems from other files while keeping conflicts tied to the target file. The Rules class returns problems rather than throwing, so exit code 2 is only triggered when a generator consumes those problems; P2.1 has no such generator, so the library behavior is acceptable.

Scope issues are recorded rather than thrown, and invalid scope shapes such as empty scopes still raise exceptions. Duplicate scope elements of equal length within a single file do not tie. FQCNs inside nowdoc and heredoc strings are correctly matched because they are String_ nodes. Concatenated FQCNs like `'Vaulter\\Drive' . '\\Node'` are not captured as single string literals, which is acceptable.

The fqcn-string regex correctly rejects non-class strings such as `Vaulter\Drive\Node\ `. Unicode class names are absent from the pattern, but this is unlikely to matter. Single-quoted backslash sequences like `'Vaulter\\Drive'` resolve to actual backslashes in the parsed string value and match the regex properly. The PHP source pattern is correctly double-encoded.

Table name matching correctly handles `v_` prefixes. A logical name like `nodes` matches directly, while `v_nodes` matches after stripping the prefix. Migration filenames such as `create_v_nodes_table.php` parse to `nodes`. The reviewer notes that a table named `v_nodes` or a logical name starting with `v_` would be unusual but handled.

The generator matches `leftJoin`, `rightJoin`, and `crossJoin` in addition to `join(`. This correctly captures real Laravel join methods that accept table names, so it is not a false positive.

`join` calls with arrays or subqueries are correctly missed. Aliased table names such as `DB::table('nodes as n')` are also missed, but the spec requires an exact string match to the table name, so this is not a violation.

Schema::create calls with variables inside migrations are correctly missed. Facade aliases and the unqualified config() helper resolve to their last segment, so they match the config rule.

Unqualified `config` calls inside namespaces still match the config rule because `isConfigCall` checks the last segment. The same holds for `Route::has` even when the facade is not imported, since the resolved class name's last segment remains `Route`.

A class named `Route` in the current namespace would falsely trigger the route rule, though this is unlikely. The generator also records `->route(` calls as route references, which could misidentify unrelated method calls; the codebase will be checked for such occurrences. `function_exists` and `extension_loaded` probes are correctly included, and `class_exists` with two arguments is handled by taking only the first argument.

Namespaced `class_exists` calls correctly resolve to the last segment. The probe handler runs before the symbol stack pops, so a call inside a method is still attributed to that enclosing method.

The symbol stack is popped before `onCall` runs, but the handler does not rely on it, so this ordering is safe.

Probe rules for `->bound(` and `->resolved(` match any receiver, which is correct. Static calls like `Foo::bound()` are also matched because the rule checks the method name rather than the call type; this is a minor extra match.

Named arguments are ignored when resolving the first positional argument for probes such as `bound`.

`new self` is correctly treated as a static reference because `self` is a Name node, not an expression. `new $this->foo` is correctly recorded as dynamic.

`instanceof` name references are correctly captured as non-dynamic. `Foo::class` inside attributes is also recorded properly. A potential visitor-order bug was noted: NameResolver replaces child nodes during traversal, which may affect how the traverser processes modified AST structures.

The visitor-order concern is resolved: NameResolver leaves FullyQualified nodes untouched, so IndexVisitor records them correctly. Attribute names like `#[Self]` are skipped as invalid. `match` expressions and PHP 8 method chaining such as `new Foo()->bar()` are handled properly.

Trait `use` statements are recorded as `name` references, not `use` imports. This separation is correct per the spec. Grouped `use` inside conditionals is illegal PHP and out of scope.

A bug was found in `onName`: for `GroupUse` nodes, the prefix is a `FullyQualified` name visited directly under `GroupUse`, not `UseItem`. Because `onName` only skips `UseItem` parents, it fails to ignore that prefix and may incorrectly record it as a class reference.

A concrete example confirms the bug: `use \Vaulter\Media\{BlobStore}` records the prefix `\Vaulter\Media` as a spurious `name` reference. That namespace prefix is not a class, so it would be misclassified and incorrectly packageOf'd by I1/I2.

The spurious `name` reference to `Vaulter\Media` from a group use would be misclassified as core by packageOf, since `Vaulter\Media` does not start with `Vaulter\Media\`. The prefix is actually a plain `Name`, not `FullyQualified`, so `onName` only records it when the leading backslash is present.

The double-counting bug is confirmed: a group use prefix with a leading backslash is recorded as a spurious class reference, while a regular single use is correctly skipped. A script will verify how common this pattern is.

A similar bug was found in namespace declarations. If the namespace name is a `FullyQualified` node, `onName` records it as a spurious `name` reference because the parent is `Namespace_`, not `UseItem`.

The namespace declaration concern is resolved. A `namespace Vaulter\Drive` declaration produces a `Name` node, not `FullyQualified`, so it is not recorded as a spurious class reference. The leading-backslash case remains the only confirmed bug.

The spurious `name` reference from a group-use prefix is a high-severity false cross-package reference. Because the prefix is not a class, `packageOf` misclassifies it as core, causing I2 to incorrectly flag the file as referencing core.

The leading-backslash group-use bug is a hard risk because it would cause false positives in all future scans once that syntax appears. Other FullyQualified nodes are correctly skipped: `\strlen()`, `\PHP_EOL`, and namespaced functions like `\Vaulter\Media\foo()` are all ignored since their parents are FuncCall or ConstFetch. `::class` references on names are recorded properly.

Trait `use` statements are correctly recorded as `name` references. Trait adaptation names such as `insteadof` are also captured properly. A trait used in both the declaration and its adaptation list may be counted twice, but this reflects a real reference occurrence and is acceptable.

`parent` is intentionally left unresolved because NameResolver does not resolve `parent`, `self`, or `static`. Tests confirm this behavior. Relative static calls such as `Sibling::foo()` are treated as name references, matching the existing `DriveModel::query()` and `Other::class` tests. The reviewer is now examining `catch` clauses that use multiple exception types separated by `|`.

Multiple exception types in `catch` clauses are correctly resolved as individual names. Nullable types such as `?D` and union returns like `F|null` are properly recorded. Default parameter values containing class constants such as `Foo::BAR` are also captured.

PHP 8.3 typed constants such as `public const Foo BAR = ...` are correctly resolved by NameResolver and visited. Property hook body references are being checked for symbol misattribution.

The allowlist logic treats violations without an explicit count as one occurrence, and it sums duplicate counts when callers pass already-counted violations; this is documented behavior.

A bug was found in the comparison logic: a violation with a different reference count is marked stale rather than new.

The comparison logic is confirmed correct: a violation with a higher reference count than allowed is properly marked stale, not new. Whitespace-only reasons are rejected by trimming, and `removed_in` set to `never` for I1 is correctly rejected.

I4 categories are correctly validated against the permanent allowlist. A potential bug was found in the `removed_in` phase logic: I1 blocks from P4, so allowing `removed_in = P5` is invalid per the spec that requires `removed_in` to be at or before the blocking phase. The reviewer is weighing whether this belongs to P2.1 scope.

The allowlist validation rule is confirmed as a finding. I1, I2, and I3 block from P4, so `removed_in = P5` is invalid. I4 blocks from P3, so `removed_in = P4` or `P5` is also invalid. The implementation currently accepts all of P3, P4, and P5 for every invariant type.

A reproduction script will confirm that `Allowlist::fromArray` accepts invalid `removed_in` values such as I1/P5 and I4/P4. Severity is medium or low because this semantic deviation does not break reference extraction, though it weakens future allowlist governance. A counterargument suggests the blocking-phase check may belong to the P2.4 scan generator rather than the generic Allowlist loader.

The reviewer resolved the earlier counterargument. Blocking-phase mappings are not stored in the allowlist JSON, so hardcoding them inside the Allowlist class is consistent with existing design choices such as REMOVED_IN and PERMANENT_CATEGORIES. The `never` exception is already implemented there, but the phase inequality check is missing. This inconsistency confirms the finding. The exact-scope bug in Rules remains valid.

The `winner` logic in Rules correctly rejects equal-length prefixes as conflicts because identical strings are already rejected at load. Scope longest-match length calculations are accurate: the `path:` prefix is excluded from the string length, and member subjects are not matched by path scopes.

Type subjects are matched by fully qualified class name scope, not by file path. A type can therefore be uncovered even if its source file lies within a scoped directory. The core-kernel unit correctly separates these two mechanisms: `Vaulter\` covers types while `path:packages/core/` covers files. A migration file inside `packages/core/database/` is properly matched by that path prefix.

A prefix rule such as `Vaulter\Access` without a trailing slash incorrectly matches `Vaulter\AccessExtra`. The spec examples use trailing slashes, so this boundary-less prefix behavior is a medium-severity bug.

The trailing-slash prefix concern is resolved. The design explicitly requires a trailing backslash to establish namespace boundaries, so `Vaulter\Access` without one matching `Vaulter\AccessExtra` is intentional author responsibility. This is not a code bug.

However, the exact-FQCN scope issue remains valid. The design distinguishes exact from prefix matching, but the implementation does not.

FQCN scope matching is exact equality. A rule for `Vaulter\Foo` does not match `Vaulter\Foo\Bar`, and member references such as `Vaulter\Foo::bar` are handled by member rules rather than FQCN rules.

Prefix rules cannot match member subjects. Members require exact member rules, which the spec mandates for each method.

Stale detection works correctly when a member rule value differs from the reference. Two member rules with identical values are treated as conflicts.

File rules with identical values are handled correctly. A longer prefix that does not match still loses to a shorter one. PHP_INT_MAX correctly separates exact and prefix matches. Two FQCN rules with different values each win their own type. Equal FQCN rules across files are treated as conflicts, but the winner is deterministic because rules are sorted by file order.

A planned package with `exists: false` and `current_require` is not overwritten by the generator. The `fromComposer` method does not sort PSR-4 keys itself; JSON encoding canonicalizes them, so fixture comparison remains stable.

A bug was found in the generator loader: it uses `require` instead of `require_once`. When a generator file is included again, the function returns `true` rather than the generator object. This causes repeated invocations to fail.

The `inv_generator()` function returns `true` on repeated calls because the generator file is already included. The test suite loops over this call, so the second invocation fails and `->check` errors. The CLI only loads each generator once per process, so it avoids this bug.

The reviewer is puzzled by the test results. The cycle test calls `inv_generator()` four times in one process, which should crash if `require` returns `true` on the second call. Because all 105 tests pass, the reviewer suspects either the tests were never actually run or PHP's `require` semantics are being misunderstood.

The reviewer realized that `require` re-executes the file every time, unlike `require_once`. This means repeated calls to `inv_generator()` should return the generator object each time, not `true`. The prior concern about a `require` bug is therefore invalid.

The reviewer is now verifying that a change to `TestRunnerTest` does not break existing functionality.

The reviewer is inspecting `TestRunnerTest` for weak assertions that could allow a test to pass even when it should fail. They also noticed that the real repository test calls `references()[0]` without first verifying the array is non-empty, which would trigger an error if references were empty.

The reviewer found no tests that cannot fail. The real repository test checks only the first reference keys, which is a minor assertion gap but not a product bug. The CLI script uses PHP_BINARY, and tests run under scripts/t with php84.

A potential name-resolution bug with attributes on anonymous classes was noted but not pursued. The reviewer confirmed that IndexVisitor records fully qualified names correctly because NameResolver resolves them in the parent node before the child is visited.

Resolved names are stored as attributes while nodes are replaced, so the default `replaceNodes` behavior is safe. Special class names such as `parent::` remain as Name nodes and are not recorded, which could hide cross-package dependencies. The design accepts this NameResolver behavior, and tests explicitly document that `self` and `static` are not treated as names.

The reviewer will probe whether `parent` is silently dropped, but NameResolver does not resolve it, so it remains excluded from the spec's resolved-name requirement. The reviewer also began checking group-use false names.

Static properties and trait imports are recorded correctly. A bug was found in group-use declarations: `use function \Vaulter\{helper};` is not handled properly.

The group-use bug creates a spurious name reference to `Vaulter`. Because the prefix `\Vaulter` is fully qualified, the parent GroupUse node is misclassified as a name reference. The package resolver returns null for this bare name, so I1 may ignore it. If the scanner treats all name references as type references, this produces a false positive.

A more serious bug was found in group-use declarations. `use \Vaulter\Media\{BlobStore}` records a name reference to `Vaulter\Media`. The package resolver returns null for this bare name, so I2 treats it as an external reference and ignores it. This causes a drive file that imports from `\Vaulter\Media` to be misclassified as core.

The reviewer is now tracing how the spurious `Vaulter\Media` reference propagates. A drive file importing from `\Vaulter\Media` would be misclassified as core, but a media file importing from `\Vaulter\Drive` would also be misclassified as core because `Vaulter\Drive` does not match the `Vaulter\Drive\` prefix. The reviewer is now probing whether a deeper nested path like `\Vaulter\Drive\Models` would also fail to match its own prefix.

A fully qualified group-use prefix such as `\Vaulter\Drive\Models` matches its own package prefix. A core file importing from drive therefore receives a false name reference to drive. This triggers a false I1 violation. The severity is high because the extractor itself is wrong regardless of style. The reviewer will confirm this with a script. They also noted that an unqualified prefix like `Vaulter\Drive\Models` would not trigger the same bug.

The leading-slash group-use bug is latent but real. The codebase typically uses unqualified group-use statements, so this pattern is unlikely to appear in practice. Non-leading-slash group use is already tested and passes.

The existing test only exercises unqualified group-use declarations, so the leading-slash variant is untested. NameResolver leaves the GroupUse prefix as a Name node when no leading backslash is present; it only converts to FullyQualified when one is present. This confirms the spurious name reference bug is limited to fully qualified group-use prefixes.

Fully qualified `new` expressions and group-use items are valid class references and are recorded correctly. The fix for the group-use prefix bug is to skip `onName` when the parent node is a `GroupUse` or `Namespace_`. This review will not apply fixes.

The reviewer is now probing the table-name extractor for false positives. Plain strings like `'nodes'` inside `->on('nodes')` and `Carbon::from('nodes')` are mis-indexed as table names. The reviewer will search the codebase for similar patterns that could break `SourceIndex::fromSources`.

The reviewer now ranks the extractor bugs by severity. The leading-slash group-use prefix is highest because it corrupts every later scan that depends on correct references. The anonymous-class method symbol is medium-high. Scope-exact fully qualified class names are medium. The table-literal extractor is also medium.

The reviewer added trait-use aliases, anonymous-class implements, nowdoc strings, and `whereTable` or `from` subqueries to the extraction probe. They also verified that interpolated `::class` inside strings is a ClassConstFetch node, so it should still register as a name reference.

The reviewer checked whether a known php-parser bug could cause IndexVisitor to record unresolved attribute names. They traced the visitor order for `#[G] class Run` and confirmed that NameResolver resolves the Attribute name before IndexVisitor records it, so this path is safe.

Method attributes are correctly attributed to the enclosing method symbol. The existing test suite does not cover this case, but the behavior is reasonable.

Property attributes are correctly attributed to the enclosing class symbol. Parameter type references inside methods inherit the method symbol, and closures within methods keep the method symbol. Enum case references are working correctly. PHP 8.4 asymmetric visibility property types still produce type nodes as expected. The pretty printer used in `SourceIndex` is deterministic, so exact string checks in tests remain valid. Fully qualified `::class` references print correctly.

The pinned php-parser ^5.7 dependency prevents pretty-printer changes between versions. Declaration order is source-order, and json_encode preserves key order, so non-determinism is ruled out. The `package` field is missing from the spec's `declarations()` guidance.

The `package` field is an extra implementation detail, not a bug. References omit it because the spec does not require it; `packageOf()` is separate. Dynamic references appear in visitor order, which is acceptable. Parse errors throw `InventoryError`, and the CLI catches them with exit code 2. A named argument bug was found in the table extractor. The `TABLE_ARGS` list includes `table`, `entity`, and `from`. The code records any call that has a named argument matching those keys. Relative class names inside namespaces are correctly converted to FullyQualified nodes and visited. Fully qualified names inside `UseItem` nodes are correctly skipped, so imports are recorded only as `use` references and never as `name` or `fqcn-string`. content.thinking: A significant finding has been identified.

A strong bug was found. `model('activity')` is a config/model key, not a table reference, but because its string matches a logical table name and the class resides under `Repositories\`, it is incorrectly recorded as `table-literal`.

The spec intends `table-literal` for table names appearing in constants or arrays without context. The implementation incorrectly records every matching string anywhere in the class, including inside `model()` arguments. This causes false positives like `model('nodes')` to be misclassified when the actual model key is `node`.

Most `model()` calls are false positives. `activity`, `scan_evidence`, and `outbox` are not table names. `node`, `drive`, `file`, `blob`, `file_revision`, and `scan_obligation` do not match their tables either. Only `node` avoids the bug because the table is `nodes`.

`webhook_endpoint`, `webhook_delivery`, `node_share`, and `file_revision_blob` are also false positives. The bug only avoids exact matches like `documents`. `ActivityReadRepository::base` and `ActivityStoreRepository::record` both incorrectly index `activity`.

ScanEvidenceRepository and OutboxStoreRepository also incorrectly index `scan_evidence` and `outbox`. KeyColumnInspector arrays and SchemaBuilder match arms are likely legitimate under the spec. The total of 148 table-literals is mostly correct usage.

The inventory generator contains 12 false table-literal references from `model('activity'|'scan_evidence'|'outbox')`.

The false table references are a real current-index bug. I1 counts table references by owner in the target view and identities, but not in core. This causes false violations or allowlist entries for tables like `activity` and `scan_evidence`.

The `inTableClass()` else-branch is the bug. It misclassifies model keys as table literals. SchemaBuilder match arms are structured literals and are not false references.

The finding will target any string in Schema or Repositories classes, not only constants and arrays. `model('activity')` reproduces the false table reference. `on` and `DB::*` strings did not produce obvious false tables in the outside list, so they are deferred to a lower severity.

The `on` matcher is a synthetic landmine. It is not observed in the current index, so it will be reported as medium/low severity or omitted.

The findings will be merged into a single "table classification" report. The real false model-key references are the primary issue. The `on` and `DB::*` matcher deviations are secondary, synthetic issues.

Config references are a real medium finding. Route `->route('token')` is another real medium finding. Anonymous symbols in migrations are a real medium finding with latent collision risk; these will be combined. Rules scope is a medium-high finding. It has no current fixtures but the semantics are wrong for P2.2 and would cause false out-of-scope rejections.

Fully qualified class name strings in tests are not being indexed.

KeyColumnInspector arrays and SchemaBuilder match arms are legitimate table literals. Anonymous class symbols correctly resolve to the enclosing method. Every create migration is affected by the `<file>` issue, so it will be reported as medium severity.

The `<file>` symbol is coarser than the method name. This is acceptable because the specification distinguishes method symbols, and anonymous classes lose their method name. The migration extends reference shares `<file>` with the SchemaBuilder class literal, but these targets differ so counts do not merge across them. Merging only occurs within the same target between up and down.

content.thinking:
I have a solid understanding of the design.

Re-running the probe script to capture exact output for the report. Also inspecting scripts/t and scripts/php84 to work around the mktemp permission failure.

I will run the targeted inventory test and report the result. If sandbox restrictions block it, I will try a substitute that avoids writing to the repository. I also need to inspect the test file for assertions that lock in buggy behavior or cannot fail.

I am grepping the real index log to confirm concrete findings: migration symbols, false config references, route tokens, and table-literal model() calls.

I also noticed a spec-implementation mismatch. The design document only requires matching `route(`, `->name(`, `Route::has(`, and `URL::route(`. The current code incorrectly matches any method named `route` or `name`, which would flag `$request->route('token')` as a hit.

`->name(` is explicitly in the spec, so Package->name('vaulter') is collateral noise, not a deviation.

The config rule is broader than the spec. The spec targets first arguments of `config(`, `Config::get`, and `->get`/`->has` on config repositories. The implementation flags any `get`/`has` call or any static `Config::*` method. Named arguments are missed because only the first positional argument is checked.

Table-literal matches are limited to constants and arrays inside Schema or Repository classes without call context.

The table-literal rule is broader than the spec. It flags any matching string inside Schema or Repository classes that is not already a table call, so `model('activity')` calls are false positives.

Anonymous class methods lack a fully qualified class name. The design document assigns `<file>` to code outside classes, but anonymous class bodies are not considered outside classes.

Anonymous class methods are assigned the outer class name or `<file>` when no outer class exists. File-level migrations inside anonymous classes therefore share a single `<file>` symbol, causing their `up` and `down` counts to merge into one. This is a real correctness bug for later scans because counts are tracked per symbol.

The anonymous class symbol collapse is a HIGH or MEDIUM-HIGH severity issue. It affects every migration scan because file-level migrations inside anonymous classes share one symbol. This causes counts to merge incorrectly and produces false new or stale results.

The merged `<file>` symbol poisons every scan that keys on file, symbol, and count. Migration basenames are identities, not type owners, so the target view cannot exclude them. The design explicitly requires symbols to be `Class::method`, making this a real defect for new and stale counts.

The config overmatch is medium-high severity. Two of eighty-one real false positives look like config keys. `vaulter.request_id` starts with `vaulter` and appears in core/src, but I1 current counts config only by package roots such as `vaulter-media.` and `vaulter-drive.`. This means the false positives will not trigger I1 current violations.

The config overmatch is a correctness bug in the extractor itself. SourceIndex records false positives as kind=config, so later scans that consume that kind will see them. The item requires every reference kind to be correct.

The table-literal overmatch is medium-high severity. Twelve real false references appear because the rule flags any matching string inside Schema or Repository classes, including `model()` keys that happen to equal table names.

The `->route(` deviation is medium severity. It is a genuine hit on `$request->route('token')`, which the spec does not list.

`model('activity')` calls in classes outside Schema or Repositories namespaces are not table-literal.

False positives are limited to the Repositories namespace. ActivityReadRepository, ActivityStoreRepository, ScanEvidenceRepository, and OutboxStoreRepository contain `model()` calls that would be flagged as table-literal. Calls in Queries, Testing, Webhooks, Models, and Doctor are not table-literal.

Re-running the probe to capture exact output for the report. Verifying index lines in the logs. The filament ActivityResource model('activity') call is not table-literal because it sits outside Schema or Repositories namespaces. AssignCorrelationId::ATTRIBUTE is a plain class constant string, not a config reference. Now checking whether any tests lock in the wrong behavior.

InventoryHarnessTest is being searched for anonymous, config, route, table-literal, scope, and removed_in references.

The index ordering is deterministic. Sources are sorted by file name. Within each file, references follow traversal order. This matches the design requirement of sorting by file then position.

Duplicate references are not merged. The log shows SchemaBuilder name and table entries appear twice for the same file, indicating the deduplication logic is broken.

The duplicate SchemaBuilder references are not merged in the raw references list. Allowlist::compare later merges them by symbol and sums counts, so two identical symbols become a single key with count 2. The real bug is that up and down are treated as the same symbol, causing distinct references to be combined into one entry. Removing down would stale the count rather than remove a distinct symbol.

Anonymous class methods inside un-named classes collapse to the `<file>` symbol. The design does not include a `<file>::method` form, so distinct methods cannot be allowlisted separately.

Nested method references are misattributed to invented symbols. For example, `Outer::bar` receives a reference that belongs to a non-existent `Outer::other`. This is the top finding with high severity because it triggers false new and stale counts on every migration and directly causes mis-attribute errors. Hard-risk name resolution cases were verified as correct.

Rules scope matching uses `str_starts_with` for all types, including exact FQCNs. The design explicitly lists exact FQCN as a scope element type, so this is a semantic deviation. It will mis-assign responsibility and falsely reject correct splits. Severity is medium-high because it breaks the mechanism even though no rule files exist yet.

The exact FQCN bug is more severe than a simple semantic deviation. Because `str_starts_with` matches any prefix, an exact FQCN like `Vaulter\Access\Actor` would also incorrectly match `Vaulter\Access\Actor\Child`. The design explicitly requires exact FQCNs to be matched literally, not as prefixes.

The prefix bug is now isolated to exact FQCNs without a trailing separator. Path prefixes correctly use `str_starts_with`. The design requires exact FQCNs to match literally.

Scope tie-breaking by length is correct. The exact FQCN bug also causes a child namespace to match both an exact parent and a longer prefix, because `str_starts_with` matches any substring.

The exact FQCN bug only causes false out-of-scope when the longer prefix scope is missing. The probe output will be re-run to provide concrete reproduction evidence. Allowlist phase blocking is also being checked against the design: I1/I2/I3 block at P4, while I4 blocks at P3.

The allowlist validator accepts invalid phase ordering. I1 entries may specify removed_in as P5, which is after the P4 blocking phase. I4 entries may specify removed_in as P4, which is after the P3 blocking phase.

I4 entries are also permitted without a category when removed_in is not never. An I4 entry with removed_in=P4 and category=activation is accepted even though P4 exceeds the P3 blocking phase.

The class comment omits the required `removed_in ≤ фаза «Блокирует с»` inequality. This is a confirmed deviation. Severity is high because it lets allowlist entries survive past their blocking phase and remain in block mode.

The allowlist phase deviation is now rated medium severity. It is a semantic gap rather than a live false scan, though the item explicitly requires this norm. The I4 category requirement is also being reconsidered; the general scans section shows category as optional in its JSON example.

The I4 section explicitly requires every probe place to carry a category, so the validator's acceptance of I4 entries without one is a confirmed deviation. A medium-severity route false positive was also found: any method named `route` is matched, including parameter names like `$request->route('token')`, which are not route targets.

The five service provider package names will be counted as route identities under I1. The `->name(` pattern is explicitly in the spec, so this is not a bug.

Config overmatch is confirmed. `Config::set` and any `->get` or `->has` calls are recorded.

A named argument miss was found: `config(key: 'vaulter.x')` is not captured because the positional check requires `name === null`. The spec says "первый аргумент", but PHP allows named arguments as the first position. Checking whether the product uses this syntax.

The table-literal scope is wider than the spec. It captures `on`, `leftJoin`, `rightJoin`, `crossJoin`, `constrained`, `hasTable`, `dropIfExists`, and any method on `Schema` or `DB`. Synthetic calls like `$q->on('nodes')` and `DB::select('nodes')` are recorded as tables. I need to verify whether real product code uses these patterns.

Promoted `protected string $table` is parsed as a Param, not a PropertyItem. No real product code uses this pattern, so it will be dropped.

The Eloquent base matcher is too broad. It chains to any class instead of only Model.

The Eloquent base matcher is a low-severity superset. It includes `User`, `Pivot`, and `MorphPivot` as valid bases, so a class extending an external `User` would be treated as an Eloquent model even though the spec requires the chain to reach `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model`. A reproduction is needed.

I am carefully examining the rules output.

The rules output reveals a scope mismatch. `Vaulter\Access\Actor` is correctly classified as exact owner core. However, the wide prefix rule for `Vaulter\Access\ActorExtra` and `Vaulter\Access\Actor\Child` incorrectly assigns them to drive because their scope is wider than their file. The member `Vaulter\Access\Actor::run` also has no rule classifying it.

The root cause is a mismatch between `responsible()` and `winner()`. `responsible()` assigns the exact file because `str_starts_with` matches the prefix. `winner()` selects the wide file because the exact FQCN rule does not match the subtypes. This creates the out-of-scope error.

The exact FQCN rule is missing its trailing slash. This causes `str_starts_with` to match `Vaulter\Access\ActorExtra` and `Vaulter\Access\Actor\Child` as children of the exact rule, while the wide prefix rule is correctly selected as the winner. A correct split would fail the check. The exact rule should probably be a strict prefix that matches children but not unrelated types.

The design document distinguishes exact FQCNs from prefixes. Exact FQCNs must match by equality, while prefixes use `str_starts_with`. A boundary-aware prefix would require the next character after the scope to be a backslash, preventing `Vaulter\Access\ActorExtra` from being misclassified as a child of `Vaulter\Access\Actor`. The exact scope should own only that single class.

The bug is confirmed. The exact FQCN scope incorrectly claims `ActorExtra` and `Actor\Child` through `str_starts_with`. This is a P2.2 parallel-unit mechanism. It is medium-high severity. No current rule files are affected. The item builds Rules for P2.2.

The longest-match winner rule makes the bug more severe. An exact FQCN scope longer than a prefix scope steals all longer names from the prefix file. This breaks the P2.2 parallel-unit mechanism.

The exact-FQCN prefix bug is ranked high. It is a real semantic deviation from the design document, though it does not yet cause a false scan of current product code.

Anonymous-class methods are ranked first. They share the outer symbol name, which is live on every migration and affects later scan keys immediately.

Count keys merge up and down. Nested mis-attributes. This is the hard-risk class (wrong attribution → false new/stale) even though the named name-resolution cases are correct.

Config kind matches any `->get`/`->has` and any `Config::*`, and ignores named arguments. Live: 2 false config refs in core/src (request attributes). Synthetic: Config::set, $cache->get, $user->has recorded; config(key:) missed.

Table-literal is any table-name string in a Schema/Repositories class, not only constants/arrays. Live: 12 `model()` calls.

Table-literal also catches synthetic assignments and exception messages. `->on(` and `DB::*` methods are synthetic-only false positives; bundle them as a lower note or separate low finding.

Route kind matches any `->route(` call, including `$request->route('token')`. The spec only lists `route(`, `->name(`, `Route::has(`, and `URL::route(`, so `->name(` must not be flagged.
